result.document_summary: Berkeley City Council Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S. amending Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.63 to prohibit the sale or use of coordinated pricing algorithms to set rents or occupancy levels for residential units.
result.notes: Document gives no explicit effective date; it was passed to print on Nov 18, 2025 (first reading, with a December 2, 2025 agenda item), so effective_date is left blank. The ordinance applies to all residential dwelling units in Berkeley with no stated exemptions on coverage. No other in-scope categories are addressed.

rules.title: Prohibition on coordinated pricing algorithms for rents and occupancy
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to sell, license or provide to Berkeley landlords, or for a landlord to use, a coordinated pricing algorithm (one using non-public competitor data less than 90 days old) to set or recommend rents or occupancy levels for residential units. Each month and each unit is a separate violation, with civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation and enforcement by the City Attorney or aggrieved tenants.
rules.key_value: Ban on coordinated pricing algorithms; civil penalty up to $1,000 per violation
rules.citation: Berkeley Municipal Code ch. 13.63 (§§ 13.63.020-13.63.040), Ordinance No. 7,992-N.S.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to all residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley and to sellers or providers of such algorithms to Berkeley landlords.
rules.exemptions_text: No coverage exemptions for buildings; the definition of coordinated pricing algorithm excludes aggregated anonymous rental data reports, tools for setting affordable-housing rent or income limits, and products used for market research for financing, appraisals, or software research, testing or training.
